issue: Body says 'Only in the Matsya and Bhāgavata Purāṇas does it [the fish] become Viṣṇu's first avatāra'. This is false. Agni Purāṇa ch. 2 narrates the fish as Hari/Viṣṇu saving Manu Vaivasvata, and AgP 49.1 opens its ten-avatāra list with Matsya. The graph's own comparison table cmp:flood-story has an Agni Purāṇa row (AgP 2.2–15) saying the fish is Viṣṇu–Nārāyaṇa. The Bhāgavata's own list (1.3.15) also does not make Matsya 'first': it is 10th there.
evidence: GRETIL Agni Purāṇa (https://gretil.sub.uni-goettingen.de/gretil/corpustei/transformations/plaintext/sa_agnipurANa.txt): ap_2.002 'matsyāvatāraṃ vakṣye 'haṃ vasiṣṭha śṛṇu vai hareḥ', ap_2.004 'manur vaivasvatas tepe', ap_49.001 'daśāvatāraṃ matsyādilakṣaṇaṃ … matsyaḥ syāt kūrmaḥ'. GRETIL BhP 1.3.15 (Matsya is 10th in the list 1.3.6–22). data/comparisons/purana.json cmp:flood-story, Agni Purāṇa row.
fix: Replace the sentence with: 'In the Purāṇas — e.g. the Matsya (1–2), Agni (2) and Bhāgavata (8.24) — the fish is Viṣṇu, and in ten-avatāra lists such as AgP 49 it stands first; the Bhāgavata adds the demon Hayagrīva who steals the Veda.' Add AgP 2 to the sources.

issue: Body says 'Gold coins of Wima Kadphises and Kaniṣka show a deity with a bull … but the Bactrian legend reads ΟΗϷΟ'. Wima's coins carry no ΟΗϷΟ label, and no Bactrian legend at all: their legends are Greek (obverse) and Kharoṣṭhī (reverse). The name label begins with Kaniṣka I. The graph's own record art:wima-kadphises-coin says exactly this: 'On Wima's own coins the deity is not labelled OHÞO; that label appears from Kaniṣka I onward'.
evidence: data/entities/material.json art:wima-kadphises-coin (details) and deity:oesho ('from Kaniṣka I onward'); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oesho; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vima_Kadphises
fix: Rewrite as: 'Gold coins of Kaniṣka I and his successors label a bull-associated, trident-bearing deity ΟΗϷΟ (Oesho) in Bactrian … Wima Kadphises' earlier coins show a similar deity without a name label, with a Kharoṣṭhī legend calling the king mahiśvara.' Drop 'Wima Kadphises and' from the ΟΗϷΟ sentence.

issue: Systemic status inflation. 244 of the temple agent's 439 assertions (56%) rest only on Wikipedia. 234 of those are marked 'verified-online' and 180 are 'high' confidence. Among them are 51 class-3 (epigraphic) and 47 class-4 claims. AGENT-CONTRACT §3.2–3.3 defines verified-online as checked against an authoritative page, and forbids Wikipedia as sole support for a high-confidence claim. In my temple sample of 35, the claims were factually right (0 errors), but 17 were Wikipedia-only verified-online/high (e.g. temple:258, 302, 202, 216, 250, 422, 199, 273, 274, 204, 69, 174, 126, 203, 286, 212, 319).
evidence: Computed over data/assertions/temple.json, counting assertions whose every SourceRef is src:wikipedia or another 'reference'-type source. I spot-read the cited Wikipedia pages (e.g. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashi_Vishwanath_Temple, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janaki_Mandir).
fix: For each Wikipedia-only assertion, either add the primary or scholarly source the Wikipedia sentence cites (ASI/UNESCO page, SII/EI volume, Michell, Harle, temple inscription edition) and keep 'verified-online', or downgrade to status 'source-checked'/'recall' and confidence 'medium'. Class-3 claims need an epigraphic edition in sources.

issue: Same systemic pattern in the material domain. 229 of 454 material assertions (50%) are supported only by Wikipedia. 214 of those are 'verified-online' and 167 are 'high'; 71 are class 3 (epigraphic). Examples: material:340 (Ravikīrti SERVES Pulakeśin II, class 3, Wikipedia only, although src:kielhorn-ei6 exists in the bibliography) and material:168 (Delhi iron pillar REFERS_TO Viṣṇu, Wikipedia only). Factual accuracy in my material sample was 22/22.
evidence: Computed over data/assertions/material.json. Kielhorn EI VI is already cited on ins:aihole-ravikirti. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aihole_inscription; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_pillar_of_Delhi
fix: Add the epigraphic edition (Kielhorn EI VI for Aihole; Fleet CII III no. 32 for the iron pillar; Fleet CII III for Eran and Udayagiri, etc.) to every class-3 assertion now resting on Wikipedia alone. Otherwise set status 'source-checked'/'recall' and confidence 'medium'.

issue: Regional entities are frequently 'recall' yet 'high' confidence: 93 of 161 regional entities, 25 of them carrying precise numeric dates (e.g. text:vikramarjuna-vijaya c. 941; person:pampa 902–c. 955; text:tukaram-gatha; deity:vitthala '1189 and 1237 CE'). The contract (§3.3) forbids high confidence on unchecked precise claims. In addition, 34 of 45 regional comparison rows are 'recall'.
evidence: Tabulated status × confidence over data/entities/regional.json and regional-new.json and data/comparisons/regional.json. The dates I spot-checked are plausible, but they are unverified by the agent's own account.
fix: Lower confidence to 'medium' on recall-status entities with precise dates until they are checked. Otherwise verify against the named sources and set 'source-checked'.

issue: 'Kṛṣṇa IDENTIFIED_WITH Vāsudeva (deity of early inscriptions)', evidence class 1/high, rationale 'Name usage in the text'. The epic calling Kṛṣṇa 'Vāsudeva' is a textual fact, but deity:vasudeva is defined as the deity of the Heliodorus/Ghosuṇḍī/Nāṇeghāṭ inscriptions. Equating that inscriptional figure with the epic hero is a scholarly inference (class 5), as epic:414, material:66 and disc:vasudeva-before-the-epic's caveat say. Class 1/high overstates it and lets the UI attach inscriptional evidence to char:krishna as if it were textual.
evidence: data/assertions/epic.json epic:413 vs epic:414 (class 5/medium) and data/discoveries.json disc:vasudeva-before-the-epic (caveat).
fix: Either re-scope epic:413 to a naming fact (e.g. qualifiers.note 'the MBh names Kṛṣṇa Vāsudeva', with evidence class 5 and confidence medium), or retarget it so that only epic:414 (class 5) carries the identification with the inscriptional deity.

issue: Dates entry: event 'construction', label '464 CE (Saṃvat 386): pillar inscription of Mānadeva', certainty 'secure'. Two problems. (1) A pillar inscription dates the pillar and attests the shrine; it does not date construction of the temple, whose pagoda the same record says was rebuilt c. 1702. (2) The material agent's ins:changu-narayan-manadeva records the 464 CE equation as 'conventional' (estimated), with an alternative 495/496 CE reading (disputed). So the temple record asserts as secure what the inscription record treats as disputed. In the material time machine this places the temple at 464 CE.
evidence: data/entities/temple.json temple:changu-narayan vs data/entities/material.json ins:changu-narayan-manadeva (dates: 'Saṃvat 386 = 464 CE (conventional)' estimated; '495/496 CE' disputed).
fix: Change the event to 'earliest dated object on site (Mānadeva pillar)', certainty 'estimated', and add the 495/496 alternative with view. Keep 'surviving-structure: c. 1702 rebuilding' as the fabric date.

issue: Material DateClaim with event 'surviving-structure' and label 'cult attested from the Licchavi period (5th–8th c. inscriptions)'. That attests the cult, not the surviving fabric; the same record dates the present building to a 1692 renovation. Because of this, the material time machine shows Paśupatinātha as a surviving structure at 400 CE (observed in the browser), and disc:legend-vs-fabric counts it among temples with 'a surviving phase from before 600 CE'.
evidence: Browser: http://localhost:5173/#/time?mode=material with the slider at 400 CE lists 'Paśupatinātha temple, Kathmandu: cult attested from the Licchavi period'. Data: data/entities/temple.json.
fix: Move the Licchavi attestation to system 'reception' (event 'earliest inscriptional attestation of the cult'). Keep 'surviving-structure: 1692 (or 1697) renovation' as the material date.

issue: A disputed DateClaim '5th–9th century CE (range of older proposals)' carries numeric start 400. The site uses the earliest material start, so the Sadāśiva appears in the material time machine at 400 CE, about 125 years before the record's own preferred estimate (c. 525–575 CE).

fix: Remove start/end from the 'older proposals' DateClaim, keeping only its label, so that the c. 525–575 estimate places the object. The site team should also make the time machine skip 'disputed' DateClaims when a non-disputed one exists.

issue: The earliest material DateClaim is 'destruction: January 1026 CE' (secure). The map rule ('points appear at the earliest material date of the surviving structure or object') therefore plots Somnath as if its fabric survived from 1026; the present temple is 1947–51. The same happens for temple:mahakaleshwar (destruction 1234–35; fabric 18th c.) and temple:koneswaram (destruction 1622–24; rebuilt 1952). The Tiruchendur 'occupation' event (1646) is a similar case.
evidence: data/entities/temple.json dates; src/lib/meta.ts materialDate(); caption in the material time machine.
fix: Record destruction and occupation events under system 'reception' (or as narrative events in details), so that the material placing date is the surviving fabric: Somnath 1951 (and the Ahilyābāī temple of 1783), Mahākāleśvara 18th c., Koṇeśvaram 1952.

issue: All three DateClaims are 'disputed'. The earliest, '3rd century BCE (Doniger)', comes from a general survey rather than an archaeological study, yet the site shows it unqualified as Śiva's 'EARLIEST DATED OBJECT OR STRUCTURE: 3rd century BCE — Gudimallam liṅga' on #/entity/deity:shiva. This also contradicts disc:proto-shiva's statement that the atlas never lets a disputed link set an 'earliest attestation'. The record's own summary says the majority view is 2nd–1st c. BCE.

issue: The earliest material DateClaim is '108 CE (if the inscription's year 30 is Śaka)', the minority reading. The time machine plots Muṇḍeśvarī at 108 CE, making it the oldest structural temple on the map, although the palaeographic view (c. 570–636 CE) is the scholarly majority.

issue: On a highly sensitive site the details say only that the 'Rām Lallā Virājmān image (installed in 1949) is retained' and that the mosque was 'demolished on 6 December 1992'. They omit that the image was placed inside the mosque on the night of 22–23 December 1949. They also omit the 2019 judgment's characterisation of these acts (the demolition 'an egregious violation of the rule of law'), and that title was decided on evidence of possession. The record is otherwise neutral; the omission reads as euphemism.
evidence: https://www.livelaw.in/top-stories/babri-mosque-demolition-an-egregious-violation-of-the-rule-of-law-wrong-committed-must-be-remedied-sc-read-judgment-149643 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Supreme_Court_verdict_on_Ayodhya_dispute

Cite src:sc-ayodhya-2019 with page or paragraph locators.

issue: (1) 'Kāśī Viśvanātha temple (1585)' is given as the date of surviving fabric. The 1585 Todar Mal temple was demolished in 1669; the surviving temple dates to 1780 (the record's own details). (2) '16 [temples] have a surviving phase from before 600 CE' counts Paśupatinātha, whose pre-600 'phase' is a cult attestation (see the temple:pashupatinath finding), and Muṇḍeśvarī through its minority 108 CE reading. (3) '17 of the 45' cannot be reproduced from the data: excluding destruction events I get 16 (start > 1500) or 19 (start ≥ 1500).

issue: 'In Guṇabhadra's Jain telling, the Adbhuta Rāmāyaṇa, the Thai Ramakien and the Lao Phra Lak Phra Lam she is born to Rāvaṇa's household and set adrift because of an omen.' The graph's own rows contradict this generalisation. In the Adbhuta row she is born to Mandodarī and found by Janaka in a sacrificial field, with no omen and no setting adrift. In the Guṇabhadra row she is abandoned in a casket and found in Janaka's realm, i.e. buried, not set adrift. The Lao row says only that she is Thôtsakane's daughter. Only the Ramakien row has an omen and setting adrift. All of these rows are 'recall'.
evidence: data/comparisons/regional.json cmp:sita-parentage rows (Uttarapurāṇa, Adbhuta, Ramakien, Phra Lak Phra Lam); regional:270/272/274 are medium/recall.
fix: Rewrite: 'In several tellings — Guṇabhadra's Uttarapurāṇa, the Adbhuta Rāmāyaṇa, the Ramakien, the Lao Phra Lak Phra Lam — she is born in Rāvaṇa's household (to Mandodarī or to Rāvaṇa); in some (e.g. the Ramakien) an omen leads to her being set adrift, in others she is buried or abandoned and found by Janaka.' Lower the discovery's confidence to low until the rows are checked.

issue: Title: 'their equation with Viṣṇu and Skanda is a later gloss'. The equation is not only a medieval commentator's gloss. Caṅkam-period texts already attach Viṣṇu–Kṛṣṇa mythology to Māyōṉ/Tirumāl (Paripāṭal hymns to Tirumāl; Mullaippāṭṭu's Trivikrama) and Skanda's birth myth and iconography to Murukaṉ (Paripāṭal 5; Tirumurukāṟṟuppaṭai). The graph's own cmp:murugan-skanda says the Paripāṭal 'know the northern myth of his birth' and that convergence occurred 'by the late Caṅkam period'.
evidence: data/comparisons/regional.json cmp:murugan-skanda (Paripāṭal and Tirumurukāṟṟuppaṭai rows and note). Project Madurai Tolkāppiyam with commentary: https://projectmadurai.org/pm_etexts/utf8/pmuni0500_01.html (gloss 'கடல்வண்ணன்' verified).
fix: Retitle: 'The oldest Tamil grammar names Māyōṉ and Cēyōṉ as lords of landscapes without myth; other Caṅkam poems already give them Viṣṇu's and Skanda's stories, and the medieval commentator glosses them so.'

issue: 'Four of these are counted among the twelve jyotirliṅgas; the buildings pilgrims enter are largely hers.' This is false for Somanātha: pilgrims enter the 1947–51 temple, and Ahilyābāī's 1783 temple is a separate building nearby (the record's own wording). It is also false for Aundha Nāganātha, whose fabric the graph dates to c. 13th c. (Seuṇa) with an 18th-c. renovation. The Grishneshwar attribution is recorded as disputed (temple:156, low; Wikipedia credits Gautamābāī Holkar). The scare quotes around 'ancient' also read as dismissive.
evidence: data/entities/temple.json temple:somnath, temple:aundha-nagnath; data/assertions/temple.json temple:156, temple:160, temple:220.
fix: Rewrite: 'She built the present Kāśī Viśvanātha (1780) and the Viṣṇupada at Gaya (1787), a separate Somanātha temple beside the old site (1783), and renovated Aundha Nāganātha; a role at Grishneshwar is disputed.' Drop the scare quotes.

issue: The title states as fact that 'Vāsudeva and Saṅkarṣaṇa were worshipped from Bactria to the Deccan'. The Bactrian point rests on the Agathocles coins. Identifying their figures with Vāsudeva and Saṅkarṣaṇa is class 5 (material:63/64). Moreover, Indian-standard coins of an Indo-Greek king found in an Aï Khanoum hoard show that he issued the images, not that the gods were worshipped in Bactria. The caveat addresses the Kṛṣṇa identification but not this.
evidence: data/assertions/material.json material:60, 63, 64; Audouin & Bernard 1974 (src:audouin-bernard-1974).
